flashcard_questions.q: When did the last remaining crimes in the UK lose the death penalty?
What is hudud in Shari’ah law?
flashcard_questions.a: Fixed punishments set by Allah in the Qur’an for the most serious offences.

flashcard_questions.q: What is qisas in Islamic law on murder?
flashcard_questions.a: Proportionate retribution for the crime committed.

flashcard_questions.q: What may a murder victim’s family accept instead of execution in Islam?
What does the principle of utility argue makes an action right?
flashcard_questions.a: That it brings the greatest happiness to the greatest number.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the sanctity of life teach about who may take a life?
flashcard_questions.a: Only God, because God created all life.

flashcard_questions.q: Which commandment do Christians use to argue against capital punishment?
What did Ezekiel 33:11 say God takes no pleasure in?
flashcard_questions.a: The death of the wicked, preferring that they turn and live.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Genesis verse is used to support the death penalty?
flashcard_questions.a: Genesis 9:6 — “Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed.”

flashcard_questions.q: What did Jesus tell the woman he saved from execution in John 8?
Why do opponents argue the death penalty allows no reformation?
flashcard_questions.a: Once executed, the offender can never change or make amends.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Muslim organisation actively opposes capital punishment?
Who was executed in 1953 for a murder he did not personally commit?
Who was the last woman executed in the UK?
What does Surah 17:33 teach about taking life?
flashcard_questions.a: “Do not take life, which Allah has made sacred, except by right.”

notes: 15 cards: 5 belief→source (Exodus 20:13, Ezekiel 33:11, Genesis 9:6, John 8, Surah 17:33), 4 term→definition (hudud, qisas, utility, sanctity of life), 3 argument→view (no reformation, blood money, Muslim Peace Fellowship), 2 case studies (Bentley, Ellis), 1 date.
